supports.excerpt: Knowing the aspect ratio for an image allows the browser to calculate and reserve sufficient space for the height and associated area. Modern best practice for setting image dimensions Because modern browsers set the default aspect ratio of images based on an image's `width` and `height` attributes, you can prevent layout shifts by setting those attributes on the image and including the preceding CSS in your style sheet. ``` ``` All browsers will then add a default aspect ratio based on the element's existing `width` and `height` attributes. This calculates an aspect ratio based on the `width` and `height` attributes before the image has loaded. It provides this information at the very start of layout calculation. As soon as an image is told to be a certain width (for example `width: 100%`), the aspect ratio is used to calculate the height. This `aspect-ratio` value is calculated by major browsers as the HTML is processed, rather than with a default User Agent style sheet (see this post for a deep dive into why), so the value is displayed a little differently. For example, Chrome displays it like this in the Styles section of the Element panel: ``` img[Attributes Style] { aspect-ratio: auto 640 / 360; } ``` Safari behaves similarly, using an HTML Attributes style source. Firefox doesn't display this calculated `aspect-ratio` at all in its Inspector panel, but does use it for layout. Tip: If you're having a hard time understanding aspect ratio, a handy calculator is available to help. For a fantastic deep-dive into aspect ratio with further thinking around responsive images, see jank-free page loading with media aspect ratios. If your image is in a container, you can use CSS to resize the image to the width of the container. We set `height: auto;` to avoid using a fixed value for the image height. ``` img { height: auto; width: 100%; } ``` What about responsive images? When working with responsive images, `srcset` defines the images you allow the browser to select between and what size each image is. To ensure `` width and height attributes can be set, each image should use the same aspect ratio.

skill_drafts.name: Set image dimensions to prevent layout shift
skill_drafts.description: Declare width and height attributes on img elements to allow browsers to calculate and reserve space before image load, preventing cumulative layout shift (CLS).
skill_drafts.objective: prevent layout shift by pre-calculating image space
applicable_signals: layout shift detected during image load
contraindications: image dimensions are truly dynamic or unknown at markup time
using CSS-only image sizing without HTML attributes
responsive images with varying aspect ratios across srcset
workflow_steps: Identify the image's intrinsic width and height (e.g., 640×360)
Add width and height attributes to the img element with these values
Include CSS rule: img { height: auto; width: 100%; } to enable responsive scaling
Verify in browser DevTools that aspect-ratio is calculated before image load
Confirm no layout shift occurs when image loads
triggers: image dimensions are known at markup time
constraints: all images in a responsive srcset must use the same aspect ratio
width and height attributes must reflect the actual image aspect ratio
CSS height: auto; must be set to allow responsive scaling
cautions: incorrect width/height values will cause distortion or unexpected spacing
aspect ratio is calculated by browsers at HTML parse time, not from User Agent stylesheets
output_contract: img element with width and height attributes set; browser calculates aspect-ratio before image load; no layout shift occurs when image loads; responsive scaling works correctly

examples.notes: Sets 16:9 aspect ratio; browser reserves 640×360 space during layout

skill_drafts.name: Ensure consistent aspect ratio across responsive image variants
skill_drafts.description: When using srcset for responsive images, verify that all image variants maintain the same aspect ratio so that HTML width/height attributes can be reliably set and prevent cumulative layout shifts.
skill_drafts.objective: maintain layout stability across multiple image sources by enforcing uniform aspect ratio
applicable_signals: use_when: using srcset attribute; multiple image variants exist; aspect ratio consistency is required for CLS prevention
contraindications: aspect ratio intentionally varies across breakpoints (art direction scenario)
art direction is the primary goal rather than responsive sizing
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify all image variants in the srcset attribute', 'detail': 'List each image file and its declared size (e.g., 640w, 1280w, 2x).'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Measure or retrieve the actual dimensions of each variant', 'detail': 'Obtain width and height in pixels for every image file referenced in srcset.'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Calculate aspect ratio for each variant', 'detail': 'Divide width by height for each image. Record the result (e.g., 1.78 for 16:9).'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Verify all ratios are identical', 'detail': 'Compare all calculated aspect ratios. If any differ, the variants are not compatible for single width/height attributes.'}

{'step': 5, 'action': 'Set width and height attributes on the element', 'detail': 'Use the dimensions of one variant (e.g., 640×360) as the HTML attributes. The browser will use the aspect ratio to calculate height when width is set to 100% or a responsive value.'}
triggers: srcset attribute is present on an element
multiple image variants are defined for different viewport sizes or pixel densities
cumulative layout shift (CLS) prevention is a requirement
constraints: All srcset image variants must share identical aspect ratio
Width and height attributes must be set on the element
Aspect ratio is calculated as width ÷ height and must be consistent across all variants
cautions: If variants have different aspect ratios, the browser cannot reliably reserve space; layout shifts will occur.
Art direction (intentional aspect ratio changes) requires a different approach; do not force uniform aspect ratio in that case.
output_contract: All srcset image variants have identical aspect ratio; HTML width and height attributes are set on the element; browser can reserve space before image load; layout remains stable across all viewport sizes and pixel densities.

examples.notes: Aspect ratios match; single width/height pair is sufficient.
